enum \doxymbox{\hyperlink{slub_8c_a763b2d58b8faaaa7419639f9d544310d}{add\+\_\+mode}}}

Enumeration Description:\+ This enumeration defines the two possible positions for adding a slab to the per-\/node partial list. ADD\+\_\+\+TO\+\_\+\+HEAD adds the slab at the beginning of the list, making it the first candidate for future allocations (hot cache), while ADD\+\_\+\+TO\+\_\+\+TAIL appends it to the end, reducing its priority. This allows the allocator to implement different policies for optimizing cache locality and fragmentation behavior. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}[2]{Enumerator}

enum \doxylink{slub_8c_a19ddf199e3e76102bb4ef74e10bc2bf0}{slab\+\_\+flags} -\/ How the slab flags bits are used. @\+SL\+\_\+locked:\+ Is locked with \doxylink{slub_8c_a402e0de6fd9cd61468204792f0fa248c}{slab\+\_\+lock()} @\+SL\+\_\+partial:\+ On the per-\/node partial list @\+SL\+\_\+pfmemalloc:\+ Was allocated from PF\+\_\+\+MEMALLOC reserves

The slab flags share space with the page flags but some bits have different interpretations. The high bits are used for information like zone/\+node/\+section.

Enumeration Description:\+ This enumeration defines the bit flags stored in a slab\textquotesingle{}s flags field (which overlays the page flags) to track the slab\textquotesingle{}s state and special properties. SL\+\_\+locked uses the PG\+\_\+locked bit to indicate that the slab is locked for exclusive access, typically used during list manipulation or when updating the slab\textquotesingle{}s freelist to prevent concurrent modifications. SL\+\_\+partial uses the PG\+\_\+workingset bit (for historical reasons) to mark that the slab is on the per-\/node partial list, indicating it has some free objects available for allocation but is not completely empty or full. SL\+\_\+pfmemalloc uses the PG\+\_\+active bit (also for historical reasons) to indicate that the slab was allocated from the PFMEMALLOC reserves, meaning its objects should be treated specially (e.\+g., not used for regular allocations or freed with extra caution) to ensure memory availability during low-\/memory conditions. These flags allow the slab allocator to encode important state information directly into the slab\textquotesingle{}s page structure without requiring additional memory, enabling fast and efficient state checks in performance-\/critical paths. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}[2]{Enumerator}

\Hypertarget{slub_8c_a941fceda51e3eafd88dec169928b92a3}\index{slub.c@{slub.c}!stat\_item@{stat\_item}}
\index{stat\_item@{stat\_item}!slub.c@{slub.c}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{stat\_item}{stat\_item}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a941fceda51e3eafd88dec169928b92a3} 
enum \doxymbox{\hyperlink{slub_8c_a941fceda51e3eafd88dec169928b92a3}{stat\+\_\+item}}}

Enumeration Description:\+ This enumeration defines all the performance and event counters tracked by the SLUB allocator when CONFIG\+\_\+\+SLUB\+\_\+\+STATS is enabled, providing detailed visibility into the allocator\textquotesingle{}s behavior for performance analysis, debugging, and tuning. The counters cover allocation paths (ALLOC\+\_\+\+FASTPATH from percpu sheaves and ALLOC\+\_\+\+SLOWPATH from partial or new slabs), free paths (FREE\+\_\+\+FASTPATH to sheaves, FREE\+\_\+\+SLOWPATH to slabs, FREE\+\_\+\+RCU\+\_\+\+SHEAF for RCU-\/deferred frees, and FREE\+\_\+\+RCU\+\_\+\+SHEAF\+\_\+\+FAIL for failures), slab management operations (FREE\+\_\+\+ADD\+\_\+\+PARTIAL when adding to partial list, FREE\+\_\+\+REMOVE\+\_\+\+PARTIAL when removing, ALLOC\+\_\+\+SLAB for new slabs from page allocator, FREE\+\_\+\+SLAB when freeing slabs back, and ALLOC\+\_\+\+NODE\+\_\+\+MISMATCH for NUMA node mismatches), sheaf and barn operations (SHEAF\+\_\+\+FLUSH, SHEAF\+\_\+\+REFILL, SHEAF\+\_\+\+ALLOC, SHEAF\+\_\+\+FREE, BARN\+\_\+\+GET, BARN\+\_\+\+GET\+\_\+\+FAIL, BARN\+\_\+\+PUT, BARN\+\_\+\+PUT\+\_\+\+FAIL, SHEAF\+\_\+\+PREFILL\+\_\+\+FAST/\+\+SLOW/\+\+OVERSIZE, and SHEAF\+\_\+\+RETURN\+\_\+\+FAST/\+\+SLOW), and error/\+fallback conditions (ORDER\+\_\+\+FALLBACK and CMPXCHG\+\_\+\+DOUBLE\+\_\+\+FAIL). The NR\+\_\+\+SLUB\+\_\+\+STAT\+\_\+\+ITEMS constant represents the total number of counters, used for sizing the stat array in struct \doxylink{structkmem__cache__stats}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+stats}. These statistics can be accessed and cleared via sysfs, making them invaluable for identifying bottlenecks, understanding allocation patterns, and optimizing the slab allocator\textquotesingle{}s performance. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}[2]{Enumerator}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{track\_item}{track\_item}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a1ab285278f6aadbcc5642de1ac8132dc} 
enum \doxymbox{\hyperlink{slub_8c_a1ab285278f6aadbcc5642de1ac8132dc}{track\+\_\+item}}}

Enumeration Description:\+ This enumeration defines the two types of tracking entries stored for objects when CONFIG\+\_\+\+SLUB\+\_\+\+DEBUG and SLAB\+\_\+\+STORE\+\_\+\+USER are enabled. TRACK\+\_\+\+ALLOC represents allocation tracking information (who allocated the object, when, and the stack trace), while TRACK\+\_\+\+FREE represents deallocation tracking information (who freed the object, when, and the stack trace). These values are used as indices into the tracking arrays stored in a slab\textquotesingle{}s object metadata, allowing the allocator to record and retrieve both allocation and free history for debugging memory leaks, use-\/after-\/free bugs, and double-\/free detection. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}[2]{Enumerator}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{\_\_kfree\_rcu\_sheaf()}{\_\_kfree\_rcu\_sheaf()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_abda848a05efa3c522557321b50343d44} 
bool \+\_\+\+\_\+kfree\+\_\+rcu\+\_\+sheaf (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{obj}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Function Description:\+ This function handles deferred freeing of an object via RCU, specifically targeting the percpu sheaf layer. It attempts to place the object into a dedicated rcu\+\_\+free sheaf for the current CPU. If no such sheaf exists, it tries to get an empty one from the spare, the barn, or by allocating a new one. Once the sheaf is full, it is queued for an RCU callback (rcu\+\_\+free\+\_\+sheaf) to be freed later. The function returns true on success, and false if it cannot find or allocate a sheaf. It is not supported on PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT kernels.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a3bb23c94982e9786c912475c939e55dc} 
int \+\_\+\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+do\+\_\+shrink (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+shrink discards empty slabs and promotes the slabs filled up most to the head of the partial lists. New allocations will then fill those up and thus they can be removed from the partial lists.

The slabs with the least items are placed last. This results in them being allocated from last increasing the chance that the last objects are freed in them.

Function Description:\+ This function is the internal implementation of \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_af4b8d568d8df7affba9555c1c67a7e1b}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+shrink()}. It iterates over all nodes and, for each node, it promotes slabs with fewer free objects to the head of the partial list. It also discards completely empty slabs. The goal is to reduce fragmentation and free up unused memory. It returns 1 if any slabs remain on any node, and 0 otherwise.

Release all resources used by a slab cache.

Function Description:\+ This is the main function for shutting down a \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}. It flushes all per-\/\+CPU caches, waits for any pending RCU sheaves, and then attempts to free all partial slabs on every node. If any slabs are still in use, it returns 1 (indicating the cache is not empty). Otherwise, it returns 0. This function must be called before the cache is destroyed.

\+\_\+\+\_\+kvmalloc\+\_\+node -\/ attempt to allocate physically contiguous memory, but upon failure, fall back to non-\/contiguous (vmalloc) allocation. @size:\+ size of the request. {\bfseries{}}:\+ which set of kmalloc buckets to allocate from. @align:\+ desired alignment. @flags:\+ gfp mask for the allocation -\/ must be compatible (superset) with GFP\+\_\+\+KERNEL. @node:\+ numa node to allocate from

Only alignments up to those guaranteed by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()} will be honored. Please see Documentation/\+core-\/api/\+memory-\/allocation.\+rst for more details.

Uses kmalloc to get the memory but if the allocation fails then falls back to the vmalloc allocator. Use kvfree for freeing the memory.

GFP\+\_\+\+NOWAIT and GFP\+\_\+\+ATOMIC are supported, the \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+NORETRY modifier is not. \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+RETRY\+\_\+\+MAYFAIL is supported, and it should be used only if kmalloc is preferable to the vmalloc fallback, due to visible performance drawbacks.

Return:\+ pointer to the allocated memory of NULL in case of failure

Function Description:\+ This is the exported \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab10c2a78159aab6499cff2027104abf4}{kvmalloc\+\_\+node()} function. It first attempts to allocate physically contiguous memory using \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()}. If that fails and the size is larger than a page, it falls back to \doxylink{vmalloc_8h_a4fa760a1e23c4b642add844f040ae713}{vmalloc()}. It adjusts the GFP flags via \doxylink{slub_8c_aa3b79d36c7bc06ded29e9f10660330b9}{kmalloc\+\_\+gfp\+\_\+adjust()} and supports various flags. The VM\+\_\+\+ALLOW\+\_\+\+HUGE\+\_\+\+VMAP flag is used to allow huge page mappings for the vmalloc fallback.

void \+\_\+\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+install\+\_\+empty\+\_\+sheaf (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslub__percpu__sheaves}{slub\+\_\+percpu\+\_\+sheaves}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{pcs}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslab__sheaf}{slab\+\_\+sheaf}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{empty}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structnode__barn}{node\+\_\+barn}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{barn}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

pcs is locked. We should have get rid of the spare sheaf and obtained an empty sheaf, while the main sheaf is full. We want to install the empty sheaf as a main sheaf, and make the current main sheaf a spare sheaf.

However due to having relinquished the cpu\+\_\+sheaves lock when obtaining the empty sheaf, we need to handle some unlikely but possible cases.

If we put any sheaf to barn here, it\textquotesingle{}s because we were interrupted or have been migrated to a different cpu, which should be rare enough so just ignore the barn\textquotesingle{}s limits to simplify the handling.

An alternative scenario that gets us here is when we fail \doxylink{slub_8c_aa8949bf1d7fa1f8d352ee16022d5eec2}{barn\+\_\+replace\+\_\+full\+\_\+sheaf()}, because there\textquotesingle{}s no empty sheaf available in the barn, so we had to allocate it by \doxylink{slub_8c_ae831b7de20f1dbd8dda6cc5c51e40467}{alloc\+\_\+empty\+\_\+sheaf()}. But because we saw the limit on full sheaves was not exceeded, we assume it didn\textquotesingle{}t change and just put the full sheaf there.

Function Description:\+ This function installs an empty sheaf as the new main sheaf for a CPU\textquotesingle{}s percpu sheaf cache. It expects the CPU\textquotesingle{}s sheaf lock to be held. In the common case where there is no spare sheaf, it makes the current main sheaf the spare and sets the empty sheaf as the new main. It also handles unlikely scenarios, such as a spare already existing or the main sheaf having space, by putting the empty sheaf back into the barn or swapping the main and spare sheaves.

Replace the empty main sheaf with a (at least partially) full sheaf.

Must be called with the cpu\+\_\+sheaves local lock locked. If successful, returns the pcs pointer and the local lock locked (possibly on a different cpu than initially called). If not successful, returns NULL and the local lock unlocked.

Function Description:\+ Replaces an empty main sheaf with a full one. Tries spare, barn, or allocates a new sheaf. Returns the pcs pointer or NULL.

struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslub__percpu__sheaves}{slub\+\_\+percpu\+\_\+sheaves}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} \+\_\+\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+replace\+\_\+full\+\_\+main (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslub__percpu__sheaves}{slub\+\_\+percpu\+\_\+sheaves}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{pcs}{, }\item[{bool}]{allow\+\_\+spin}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Replace the full main sheaf with a (at least partially) empty sheaf.

Must be called with the cpu\+\_\+sheaves local lock locked. If successful, returns the pcs pointer and the local lock locked (possibly on a different cpu than initially called). If not successful, returns NULL and the local lock unlocked.

Function Description:\+ This function is called when a CPU\textquotesingle{}s main sheaf is full and needs to be replaced with an empty or partially empty sheaf. It first attempts to get an empty sheaf from the barn. If no empty sheaf is available, it tries to allocate a new one. If the barn is full of full sheaves, it may flush one. The function handles lock contention and fallback scenarios, returning a pointer to the updated percpu sheaf structure or NULL if it cannot complete the replacement.

Function Description:\+ This is the internal function for \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ac8c9ea33aa7b9f664e1a395d4db27399}{krealloc()}. It checks if the existing allocation is large enough for the new size and if the alignment matches. If so, it reuses the existing memory, optionally zeroing the new space. If not, it allocates new memory, copies the old data, and returns the new pointer. It handles both slab and large kmalloc allocations. The caller is responsible for freeing the old pointer if a new one is returned.

Function Description:\+ This function attempts to refill objects from any remote NUMA node that has partial slabs. It is used as a fallback when the local node is empty. It respects the remote\+\_\+node\+\_\+defrag\+\_\+ratio to avoid excessive remote allocations. It iterates over zones and nodes allowed by cpuset and calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a1f15cff6cdad9cc08fb301bf226114f2}{\+\_\+\+\_\+refill\+\_\+objects\+\_\+node()} for each node.

unsigned int \+\_\+\+\_\+refill\+\_\+objects\+\_\+node (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p}{, }\item[{gfp\+\_\+t}]{gfp}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{min}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{max}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{n}{, }\item[{bool}]{allow\+\_\+spin}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Function Description:\+ This function refills an array of objects from a specific NUMA node\textquotesingle{}s partial list. It takes a list of slabs from the node\textquotesingle{}s partial list and, for each slab, extracts objects from its freelist into the provided array. If a slab has more objects than needed, the remaining objects are freed back to the slab. Any slabs that were partially used are put back on the node\textquotesingle{}s partial list, and empty slabs that exceed the minimum partial limit are discarded.

unsigned int \+\_\+\+\_\+sheaf\+\_\+flush\+\_\+main\+\_\+batch (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Free all objects from the main sheaf. In order to perform \doxylink{slub_8c_aafbed8a8e0ab23f54b5401124fcec68f}{\+\_\+\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+free\+\_\+bulk()} outside of cpu\+\_\+sheaves-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}lock, work in batches where object pointers are moved to a on-\/stack array under the lock. To bound the stack usage, limit each batch to PCS\+\_\+\+BATCH\+\_\+\+MAX.

Must be called with s-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}cpu\+\_\+sheaves-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}lock locked, returns with the lock unlocked.

Returns how many objects are remaining to be flushed

Function Description:\+ Flushes a batch (up to 32 objects) from the main sheaf. Copies objects to a stack array, releases the lock, and calls bulk free. Returns remaining objects count.

void \+\_\+\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslab}{slab}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{slab}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{head}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{tail}{, }\item[{int}]{cnt}{, }\item[{unsigned long}]{addr}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Slow path handling. This may still be called frequently since objects have a longer lifetime than the cpu slabs in most processing loads.

So we still attempt to reduce cache line usage. Just take the slab lock and free the item. If there is no additional partial slab handling required then we can return immediately.

Function Description:\+ This is the slow path handler for freeing an object from a slab. It attempts to update the slab\textquotesingle{}s freelist in a loop using a cmpxchg operation. If the slab becomes empty or was previously full, it might need to be added to or removed from the per-\/node partial list, which requires taking the node\textquotesingle{}s list\+\_\+lock. The function handles these complex list management operations and, if the slab becomes completely empty and the node already has enough partial slabs, it will discard the slab back to the page allocator.

Function Description:\+ Adds a new allocation or free location to the tracking structure. It performs a binary search to find if the location (based on address, stack handle, and waste) already exists. If found, it updates the statistics (count, timing, PID, CPU, node). Function Description:\+ This function allocates per-\/\+CPU statistics storage for a \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache} when CONFIG\+\_\+\+SLUB\+\_\+\+STATS is enabled. It first uses BUILD\+\_\+\+BUG\+\_\+\+ON() to ensure at compile time that the early dynamic percpu area is large enough to accommodate statistics for all kmalloc cache types and sizes, preventing runtime allocation failures during early boot. It then calls alloc\+\_\+percpu() to allocate a struct \doxylink{structkmem__cache__stats}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+stats} for each CPU, which stores various performance counters (allocations, frees, partial list operations, sheaf operations, etc.) for the cache. If the allocation succeeds, it returns 1; otherwise, it returns 0 to indicate failure. This function is called during cache creation to enable statistics collection, which can be accessed via sysfs for performance monitoring and debugging purposes.

Function Description:\+ This function is used during early boot to "{}bootstrap"{} a static \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache} structure into a dynamically allocated one. It copies the static cache\textquotesingle{}s data into a new allocation, fixes up the slab\+\_\+cache pointers on all its slabs, and adds the new cache to the list of caches. This allows the slab allocator to be initialized from static data.

Function Description:\+ This function is called during boot to initialize the sheaves and barns for kmalloc caches after the kmalloc infrastructure itself is available. It calculates the sheaf capacity, allocates barns for each node, and allocates an initial empty sheaf for each CPU. If any allocation fails, it panics.

int build\+\_\+detached\+\_\+freelist (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{size\+\_\+t}]{size}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structdetached__freelist}{detached\+\_\+freelist}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{df}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [inline]}, {\ttfamily [static]}}

This function progressively scans the array with free objects (with a limited look ahead) and extract objects belonging to the same slab. It builds a detached freelist directly within the given slab/\+objects. This can happen without any need for synchronization, because the objects are owned by running process. The freelist is build up as a single linked list in the objects. The idea is, that this detached freelist can then be bulk transferred to the real freelist(s), but only requiring a single synchronization primitive. Look ahead in the array is limited due to performance reasons.

Function Description:\+ This function builds a detached freelist from an array of objects to be freed. It looks for objects belonging to the same slab (or same \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}) and links them together using the object\textquotesingle{}s freepointer. It takes a limited "{}lookahead"{} for performance. The result is a freelist that can be bulk-\/freed with a single lock operation. It also handles large kmalloc objects.

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{calc\_slab\_order()}{calc\_slab\_order()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a8924921c9423976774e8ff77ef9d693d} 
unsigned int calc\+\_\+slab\+\_\+order (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{unsigned int}]{size}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{min\+\_\+order}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{max\+\_\+order}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{fract\+\_\+leftover}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [inline]}, {\ttfamily [static]}}

Calculate the order of allocation given an slab object size.

The order of allocation has significant impact on performance and other system components. Generally order 0 allocations should be preferred since order 0 does not cause fragmentation in the page allocator. Larger objects be problematic to put into order 0 slabs because there may be too much unused space left. We go to a higher order if more than 1/\+16th of the slab would be wasted.

In order to reach satisfactory performance we must ensure that a minimum number of objects is in one slab. Otherwise we may generate too much activity on the partial lists which requires taking the list\+\_\+lock. This is less a concern for large slabs though which are rarely used.

slab\+\_\+max\+\_\+order specifies the order where we begin to stop considering the number of objects in a slab as critical. If we reach slab\+\_\+max\+\_\+order then we try to keep the page order as low as possible. So we accept more waste of space in favor of a small page order.

Higher order allocations also allow the placement of more objects in a slab and thereby reduce object handling overhead. If the user has requested a higher minimum order then we start with that one instead of the smallest order which will fit the object.

Function Description:\+ This function calculates the order (page size) for a slab given an object size, a minimum and maximum order, and a fractional leftover limit. It iterates from min\+\_\+order to max\+\_\+order and selects the first order where the wasted space (remainder) is less than or equal to 1/\+fract\+\_\+leftover of the slab size. This is used to determine the optimal order for a slab cache.

Function Description:\+ This function determines the final order for a slab cache. It calculates a min\+\_\+objects based on the number of CPUs, then a minimum order to fit min\+\_\+objects \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} size. It then tries to find the best order by iteratively relaxing the acceptable waste fraction (from 1/\+16 to 1/\+2). If no order is found, it falls back to the order that fits a single object. This function is key to balancing performance (locking overhead) and memory fragmentation.

int calculate\+\_\+sizes (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache__args}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+args}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{args}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

\doxylink{slub_8c_a88fc6a7cdfa2b2904854684cab29614a}{calculate\+\_\+sizes()} determines the order and the distribution of data within a slab object.

Function Description:\+ This is a core function that calculates the final layout of a slab cache. It determines the object size, alignment, inuse size, free pointer offset, red zone padding, and other metadata. It calculates the slab order and the number of objects per slab. It also sets the sheaf capacity if the cache is not a debug cache. This function is essential for creating a new \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}.

\+[Left redzone padding]\+ (if SLAB\+\_\+\+RED\+\_\+\+ZONE)

\+[Object bytes]\+ (object address starts here)

Function Description:\+ This is a comparison function used for sorting location entries in the \doxylink{structloc__track}{loc\+\_\+track}. It compares two location structures by their count field in descending order (larger counts first). This is used with the sort() function to order the allocation/\+free locations by frequency, making the most common locations appear first in the debugfs output. The cmp\+\_\+int() function returns a negative value if loc2-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}count is greater than loc1-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}count, resulting in descending sort order.

Function Description:\+ This function is a barrier for deferred frees. It synchronously waits for all pending irq\+\_\+work on all CPUs that process deferred objects to complete. This is used to ensure all deferred frees are processed before, for example, a cache is destroyed or a module is unloaded.

\doxylink{slab__common_8c_a2268455e48709f6d6c4a942ca4023507}{kvfree\+\_\+call\+\_\+rcu()} can be called while holding a raw\+\_\+spinlock\+\_\+t. Since \doxylink{slub_8c_abda848a05efa3c522557321b50343d44}{\+\_\+\+\_\+kfree\+\_\+rcu\+\_\+sheaf()} may acquire a spinlock\+\_\+t (sleeping lock on PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT), this would violate lock nesting rules. Therefore, \doxylink{slab__common_8c_a2268455e48709f6d6c4a942ca4023507}{kvfree\+\_\+call\+\_\+rcu()} avoids this problem by bypassing the sheaves layer entirely on PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT.

However, lockdep still complains that it is invalid to acquire spinlock\+\_\+t while holding raw\+\_\+spinlock\+\_\+t, even on !\+PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT where spinlock\+\_\+t is a spinning lock. Tell lockdep that acquiring spinlock\+\_\+t is valid here by temporarily raising the wait-\/type to LD\+\_\+\+WAIT\+\_\+\+CONFIG. \Hypertarget{slub_8c_a7d8078f6f2d6b8788b4dd024b5aa0c9b}\index{slub.c@{slub.c}!discard\_slab@{discard\_slab}}

Function Description:\+ This is the main function for creating a new \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}. It takes a name, size, and various arguments and flags. It calculates the sizes and order, initializes the per-\/node structures, allocates percpu sheaves, and adds the cache to sysfs. It handles early boot and normal operation. This is called by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_adf8cdc761f51d67846ff22c9b5798a58}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+create()} and other cache creation functions.

Functions provided by the slab allocators

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{early\_kmem\_cache\_node\_alloc()}{early\_kmem\_cache\_node\_alloc()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_ae76acc39ef92d4f0310fa6bdd9484021} 
void early\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node\+\_\+alloc (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{int}]{node}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

No kmalloc\+\_\+node yet so do it by hand. We know that this is the first slab on the node for this slabcache. There are no concurrent accesses possible.

Note that this function only works on the \doxylink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node} when allocating for the \doxylink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node}. This is used for bootstrapping memory on a fresh node that has no slab structures yet.

Function Description:\+ This function is used during boot to allocate and initialize a \doxylink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node} structure for a specific node before the full kmalloc infrastructure is available. It uses \doxylink{slub_8c_ae1da11965135fb966370906c07198c04}{new\+\_\+slab()} directly on the \doxylink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node} cache and manually sets up the slab and its freelist. This allows the slab allocator to bootstrap itself on new nodes. 

Definition at line \doxymbox{\hyperlink{slub_8c_source_l08306}{8306}} of file \doxymbox{\hyperlink{slub_8c_source}{slub.\+c}}.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a3854a0dda7b798b836f11177f7f9c214} 
void free\+\_\+deferred\+\_\+objects (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct irq\+\_\+work \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{work}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

In PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT irq\+\_\+work runs in per-\/cpu kthread, so it\textquotesingle{}s safe to take sleeping spin\+\_\+locks from \doxylink{slub_8c_a7538fb31a45f2685eb03ef2c5c42ef78}{\+\_\+\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free()}. In !\+PREEMPT\+\_\+\+RT irq\+\_\+work will run after local\+\_\+unlock\+\_\+irqrestore().

Function Description:\+ This function is the irq\+\_\+work callback for processing objects that were deferred for freeing from atomic or NMI contexts. It retrieves the linked list of deferred objects, iterates through them, and calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a7538fb31a45f2685eb03ef2c5c42ef78}{\+\_\+\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free()} for each one. Before freeing, it clears the freepointer to avoid false corruption reports. This allows \doxylink{slub_8c_a7955454e2c096dd76fcccb69ca765c16}{kfree\+\_\+nolock()} to be used in contexts where direct freeing is not safe.

Function Description:\+ This function attempts to free all partial slabs on a node for a given cache. It takes the list\+\_\+lock, iterates over the partial list, and moves completely empty slabs to a discard list. Any non-\/empty slabs are reported as leaks via \doxylink{slub_8c_a79c4b7a9d3477efd7621c8e1d31d0e11}{list\+\_\+slab\+\_\+objects()}. {\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a8db063671336dc1965b347f60fcb8bdc} 
bool free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{object}{, }\item[{bool}]{allow\+\_\+spin}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Free an object to the percpu sheaves. The object is expected to have passed \doxylink{slub_8c_a232beb6a2fef05c644a440a3907a321d}{slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+hook()} already.

Function Description:\+ This is the fastpath for freeing an object to the per-\/\+CPU sheaves. It acquires the CPU\textquotesingle{}s sheaf lock and checks if the main sheaf is full. If it is, it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a4f36913fa3202ab2cb1d7e8a7e4f78fa}{\+\_\+\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+replace\+\_\+full\+\_\+main()} to get a sheaf with space. It then adds the object to the main sheaf, increments its size, and releases the lock. The function returns true on success, and false if it cannot acquire the lock or find space.

void free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+bulk (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{size\+\_\+t}]{size}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Bulk free objects to the percpu sheaves. Unlike \doxylink{slub_8c_a8db063671336dc1965b347f60fcb8bdc}{free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs()} this includes the calls to all necessary hooks and the fallback to freeing to slab pages.

Function Description:\+ This function is the bulk version of \doxylink{slub_8c_a8db063671336dc1965b347f60fcb8bdc}{free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs()}. It frees an array of objects to the percpu sheaves, handling necessary hooks (memcg, alloc tagging, slab free hook) and NUMA considerations. It batches objects that belong to the same node and non-\/pfmemalloc slabs. It then attempts to free them to the per-\/\+CPU sheaves in batches. If it cannot get space in the sheaves, it falls back to the slow path (\+\_\+\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+free\+\_\+bulk). Objects that are remote or pfmemalloc are handled separately in the slow path.

Function Description:\+ Encodes a freelist pointer with obfuscation for security. It XORs the pointer with the cache\textquotesingle{}s random value and swabs the address. Used to harden freelist pointers against attacks.

struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structnode__barn}{node\+\_\+barn}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} get\+\_\+barn (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [inline]}, {\ttfamily [static]}}

Get the barn of the current cpu\textquotesingle{}s closest memory node. It may not exist on systems with memoryless nodes but without CONFIG\+\_\+\+HAVE\+\_\+\+MEMORYLESS\+\_\+\+NODES

Function Description:\+ This inline function retrieves the \doxylink{structnode__barn}{node\+\_\+barn} structure associated with the current CPU\textquotesingle{}s closest memory node for a given \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}. It calls \doxylink{slub_8c_abb2ef46ee0dbc91c6e916ba928935651}{get\+\_\+node()} with numa\+\_\+mem\+\_\+id() (which returns the NUMA node ID of the current CPU\textquotesingle{}s local memory) to obtain the per-\/node structure, and then returns the barn field from that node. The barn is used in the sheaf-\/based allocation/\+free path to manage collections of sheaves (batches of objects) across nodes, helping to reduce contention and improve scalability. If the node structure doesn\textquotesingle{}t exist (e.\+g., on systems with memoryless nodes without proper configuration), it returns NULL. This function is critical for the fastpath allocation and free operations to locate the appropriate barn for sheaf management.

Function Description:\+ This inline function retrieves the per-\/node \doxylink{structkmem__cache__node}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+node} structure for a given \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache} and NUMA node ID. It simply returns the pointer stored in s-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}node\+[node]\+, which is an array indexed by node ID containing the node-\/specific data for that cache (such as the partial slab list, statistics, and barn pointer). Function Description:\+ This function populates a struct slabinfo with statistics for a given \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}. It iterates over all NUMA nodes associated with the cache, accumulating the total number of slabs, total objects, and an approximate count of free objects (using \doxylink{slub_8c_ae8bc19bfbec4a86e3bfc27161589f90f}{count\+\_\+partial\+\_\+free\+\_\+approx()} which provides a fast but potentially inexact count). It then calculates active objects as total objects minus free objects. The function also fills in the number of objects per slab and the cache\textquotesingle{}s page order from the cache\textquotesingle{}s oo (order/\+objects) field. This is used by the /\+proc/\+slabinfo interface to provide detailed memory usage statistics for each slab cache.

Function Description:\+ This function handles the cleanup for slabs where object extension allocation previously failed. When obj\+\_\+exts equals the sentinel value OBJEXTS\+\_\+\+ALLOC\+\_\+\+FAIL, it indicates that the slab was marked as having a failed extension allocation. In this case, the function iterates over all objects in the slab and sets their code tag references to empty using set\+\_\+codetag\+\_\+empty(). This prevents false warnings or errors later when the system checks for missing metadata, ensuring that objects without extensions are properly recognized and handled. The function is called after the extension vector is freed to clean up any stale references that might cause incorrect tracking or warnings.

Function Description:\+ This inline function initializes the object extensions pointer for a slab by setting slab-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}obj\+\_\+exts to 0 (NULL). The obj\+\_\+exts field is used to store per-\/object metadata such as memcg ownership information or allocation tagging data when CONFIG\+\_\+\+SLAB\+\_\+\+OBJ\+\_\+\+EXT is enabled. By setting it to zero during slab initialization (e.\+g., when a new slab is allocated), it ensures that the slab starts with no extension metadata attached, and any subsequent allocation or freeing operations can determine whether extensions need to be allocated or managed for objects in this slab. This is a simple but critical step in maintaining the integrity of the slab\textquotesingle{}s object extension tracking system.

Can be called while holding raw\+\_\+spinlock\+\_\+t or from IRQ and NMI, but ONLY for objects allocated by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a5869820842a9951b09600f4ee9f838d9}{kmalloc\+\_\+nolock()}. Debug checks (like kmemleak and kfence) were skipped on allocation, hence obj = \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()}; kfree\+\_\+nolock(obj); will miss kmemleak/\+kfence book keeping and will cause false positives. large\+\_\+kmalloc is not supported either.

Function Description:\+ This function is a special variant of \doxylink{slub_8c_a97d9c37b943449ab48e32c6d2499261f}{kfree()} for objects allocated with \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a5869820842a9951b09600f4ee9f838d9}{kmalloc\+\_\+nolock()}. It can be called from atomic, interrupt, or NMI contexts. It skips many of the usual debugging checks (like kmemleak) that take locks. It attempts to use the fastpath \doxylink{slub_8c_a8db063671336dc1965b347f60fcb8bdc}{free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs()} (without spinning) and if that fails, it defers the free via \doxylink{slub_8c_a8f138aedda49f4d1913e086cabbee81a}{defer\+\_\+free()}. It does not support large kmalloc allocations.

It adds \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+NOWARN, removes \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+DIRECT\+\_\+\+RECLAIM unless \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+RETRY\+\_\+\+MAYFAIL is set, and removes \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+NOFAIL (as the vmalloc fallback handles this). kmalloc\+\_\+nolock -\/ Allocate an object of given size from any context. @size:\+ size to allocate @gfp\+\_\+flags:\+ GFP flags. Only \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ACCOUNT, \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO, \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+NO\+\_\+\+OBJ\+\_\+\+EXT allowed. @node:\+ node number of the target node.

Return:\+ pointer to the new object or NULL in case of error. NULL does not mean EBUSY or EAGAIN. It means ENOMEM. There is no reason to call it again and expect !\+NULL.

Function Description:\+ kmalloc that can be called from NMI/\+atomic contexts. Only supports cmpxchg\+\_\+double architectures. Returns the object or NULL.

Function Description:\+ Allocates memory without taking locks. This is used in contexts where locks are already held or not needed. It is a lockless version of \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()}.

Note that interrupts must be enabled when calling this function and gfp flags must allow spinning.

Function Description:\+ This is the exported function for allocating multiple objects from a cache. It handles the KFENCE allocation (at most one per batch), attempts to get objects from the percpu sheaves using \doxylink{slub_8c_ab731f033d4b70d794faa71b01e93fbb3}{alloc\+\_\+from\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+bulk()}, and fills the rest using \doxylink{slub_8c_a91be793dbf4641469e7732fb02732833}{\+\_\+\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+alloc\+\_\+bulk()}. It then applies post-\/alloc hooks and memory initialization. It returns the number of successfully allocated objects.

Function Description:\+ Allocates multiple objects from a kmem cache in bulk without allocation profiling. This is more efficient than allocating objects individually. Returns the number of objects successfully allocated.

Guaranteed not to fail as many allocations as was the requested size. After the sheaf is emptied, it fails -\/ no fallback to the slab cache itself.

The gfp parameter is meant only to specify \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO or \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ACCOUNT memcg charging is forced over limit if necessary, to avoid failure.

It is possible that the allocation comes from kfence and then the sheaf size is not decreased.

Function Description:\+ Allocates from a pre-\/filled sheaf. Guaranteed not to fail up to the sheaf\textquotesingle{}s size. Returns the object or NULL.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a720e99cf4604474392f2669fef155930} 
bool kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+charge (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{objp}{, }\item[{gfp\+\_\+t}]{gfpflags}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Function Description:\+ Charges an already allocated slab object to memcg. Used for late charging when allocation-\/time charging wasn\textquotesingle{}t possible.

kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+charge -\/ memcg charge an already allocated slab memory @objp:\+ address of the slab object to memcg charge @gfpflags:\+ describe the allocation context

kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+charge allows charging a slab object to the current memcg, primarily in cases where charging at allocation time might not be possible because the target memcg is not known (i.\+e. softirq context)

The objp should be pointer returned by the slab allocator functions like kmalloc (with \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ACCOUNT in flags) or kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+alloc. The memcg charge behavior can be controlled through gfpflags parameter, which affects how the necessary internal metadata can be allocated. Including \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+NOFAIL denotes that overcharging is requested instead of failure, but is not applied for the internal metadata allocation.

There are several cases where it will return true even if the charging was not done:\+ More specifically:\+


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item For !\+CONFIG\+\_\+\+MEMCG or cgroup\+\_\+disable=memory systems.
\item Already charged slab objects.
\item For slab objects from KMALLOC\+\_\+\+NORMAL caches -\/ allocated by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()} without \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ACCOUNT
\item Allocating internal metadata has failed
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

Return:\+ true if charge was successful otherwise false.

Function Description:\+ This is the exported function for bulk freeing objects from a \doxylink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}. If the cache supports sheaves, it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a5aa401003662200c843ac199bd8e7409}{free\+\_\+to\+\_\+pcs\+\_\+bulk()}. Otherwise, it repeatedly builds detached freelists and calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a9ebc0f21c24b2244a71bd986c50e8f35}{slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+bulk()} to free them.

Bulk allocation and freeing operations. These are accelerated in an allocator specific way to avoid taking locks repeatedly or building metadata structures unnecessarily.

Note that interrupts must be enabled when calling these functions.

Function Description:\+ Frees multiple objects back to a kmem cache in bulk. This is more efficient than freeing objects individually. It takes an array of pointers and frees them all.

Function Description:\+ This function is called after the rest of the kernel is initialized to perform any late initialization. int kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+refill\+\_\+sheaf (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{gfp\+\_\+t}]{gfp}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structslab__sheaf}{slab\+\_\+sheaf}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{sheafp}{, }\item[{unsigned int}]{size}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

refill a sheaf previously returned by kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+prefill\+\_\+sheaf to at least the given size

the sheaf might be replaced by a new one when requesting more than s-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}sheaf\+\_\+capacity objects if such replacement is necessary, but the refill fails (returning -\/ENOMEM), the existing sheaf is left intact

In practice we always refill to full sheaf\textquotesingle{}s capacity.

Function Description:\+ Refills a sheaf to a given size. Handles both regular and oversize sheafs. Returns 0 on success or -\/ENOMEM.

Function Description:\+ Refills a sheaf with more objects from a cache. It adds objects to an existing sheaf up to the specified size. Returns 0 on success or an error code.

Use this to return a sheaf obtained by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ac6fb041f45320469bf732b95eb27ae04}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+prefill\+\_\+sheaf()}

If the sheaf cannot simply become the percpu spare sheaf, but there\textquotesingle{}s space for a full sheaf in the barn, we try to refill the sheaf back to the cache\textquotesingle{}s sheaf\+\_\+capacity to avoid handling partially full sheaves.

If the refill fails because gfp is e.\+g. GFP\+\_\+\+NOWAIT, or the barn is full, the sheaf is instead flushed and freed.

Function Description:\+ Returns a sheaf to the cache (spare or barn). Refills the sheaf if possible, otherwise flushes and frees it.

Function Description:\+ Returns a sheaf to a cache. This frees the sheaf or returns it to the per-\/node barn for reuse. Called when a sheaf is no longer needed.

krealloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align -\/ reallocate memory. The contents will remain unchanged. {\ttfamily }:\+ object to reallocate memory for. @new\+\_\+size:\+ how many bytes of memory are required. @align:\+ desired alignment. @flags:\+ the type of memory to allocate. @nid:\+ NUMA node or NUMA\+\_\+\+NO\+\_\+\+NODE

If {\ttfamily is} NULL, \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ac8c9ea33aa7b9f664e1a395d4db27399}{krealloc()} behaves exactly like \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()}. If @new\+\_\+size is 0 and {\ttfamily is} not a NULL pointer, the object pointed to is freed.

Only alignments up to those guaranteed by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()} will be honored. Please see Documentation/\+core-\/api/\+memory-\/allocation.\+rst for more details.

If \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO logic is requested, callers must ensure that, starting with the initial memory allocation, every subsequent call to this API for the same memory allocation is flagged with \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO. Otherwise, it is possible that \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO is not fully honored by this API.

When \doxylink{mm_2slab_8h_a50a3617883868e5066bd41b61e3e568d}{slub\+\_\+debug\+\_\+orig\+\_\+size()} is off, \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ac8c9ea33aa7b9f664e1a395d4db27399}{krealloc()} only knows about the bucket size of an allocation (but not the exact size it was allocated with) and hence implements the following semantics for shrinking and growing buffers with \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO:\+:\+ \begin{DoxyVerb}      new             bucket
\end{DoxyVerb}
 0 size size \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/---\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/-\/---\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} keep \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} zero \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}

Otherwise, the original allocation size \textquotesingle{}orig\+\_\+size\textquotesingle{} could be used to precisely clear the requested size, and the new size will also be stored as the new \textquotesingle{}orig\+\_\+size\textquotesingle{}.

In any case, the contents of the object pointed to are preserved up to the lesser of the new and old sizes.

Return:\+ pointer to the allocated memory or NULL in case of error

Function Description:\+ This is the exported function for reallocating memory, with the ability to specify a NUMA node and alignment. It handles the case where new\+\_\+size is 0 by freeing the old pointer and returning ZERO\+\_\+\+SIZE\+\_\+\+PTR. It calls \+\_\+\+\_\+do\+\_\+krealloc() to perform the reallocation and frees the old pointer if a new one is allocated. This is the no-\/profile version of the function.

Common kmalloc functions provided by all allocators

Function Description:\+ Reallocates memory with alignment and node affinity without allocation profiling. It changes the size of a previously allocated memory block, preserving the contents up to the smaller size. This is the internal implementation for krealloc with alignment.

This should only be used internally to query the true size of allocations. It is not meant to be a way to discover the usable size of an allocation after the fact. Instead, use \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a2b814faa932a75fad705b1b9d5e5d630}{kmalloc\+\_\+size\+\_\+roundup()}. Return:\+ size of the actual memory used by @objp in bytes

Function Description:\+ This is the exported function to report the full size of an underlying allocation. It first validates the pointer with KASAN. It calls \doxylink{slub_8c_afc8dc4d447e2fcaf0835cf292ed1a52d}{\+\_\+\+\_\+ksize()} to get the size. This function should not be used to discover usable size; use \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a2b814faa932a75fad705b1b9d5e5d630}{kmalloc\+\_\+size\+\_\+roundup()} instead.

kvfree\+\_\+sensitive -\/ Free a data object containing sensitive information. @addr:\+ address of the data object to be freed. @len:\+ length of the data object.

Use the special memzero\+\_\+explicit() function to clear the content of a kvmalloc\textquotesingle{}ed object containing sensitive data to make sure that the compiler won\textquotesingle{}t optimize out the data clearing.

Function Description:\+ This function is used to free sensitive data (like cryptographic keys) allocated with \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_aacbb1d218fb9bc08259e0b2a0ec39701}{kvmalloc()}. It first zeroes out the memory using memzero\+\_\+explicit() to prevent the compiler from optimizing away the clear, and then calls \doxylink{slub_8c_ac88c4c777e1cffcd536d365ce527ba94}{kvfree()} to free the memory.

kvrealloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align -\/ reallocate memory; contents remain unchanged {\ttfamily }:\+ object to reallocate memory for @size:\+ the size to reallocate @align:\+ desired alignment @flags:\+ the flags for the page level allocator @nid:\+ NUMA node id

If {\ttfamily is} NULL, \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ae4cb7883b03514294e90e96af0bff095}{kvrealloc()} behaves exactly like \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_aacbb1d218fb9bc08259e0b2a0ec39701}{kvmalloc()}. If @size is 0 and {\ttfamily is} not a NULL pointer, the object pointed to is freed.

Only alignments up to those guaranteed by \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ab39d1834eaedb0985332521b254f2e01}{kmalloc()} will be honored. Please see Documentation/\+core-\/api/\+memory-\/allocation.\+rst for more details.

If \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO logic is requested, callers must ensure that, starting with the initial memory allocation, every subsequent call to this API for the same memory allocation is flagged with \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO. Otherwise, it is possible that \+\_\+\+\_\+\+GFP\+\_\+\+ZERO is not fully honored by this API.

In any case, the contents of the object pointed to are preserved up to the lesser of the new and old sizes.

This function must not be called concurrently with itself or \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_ac88c4c777e1cffcd536d365ce527ba94}{kvfree()} for the same memory allocation.

Return:\+ pointer to the allocated memory or NULL in case of error

Function Description:\+ This is the exported function for reallocating memory, similar to \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a1956cee497c6e0aa3b0e0d61842c2b0c}{krealloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align\+\_\+noprof()}, but it can also handle vmalloc-\/allocated memory. If the existing pointer is from vmalloc, it calls \doxylink{vmalloc_8h_a5e8f69c662b265347214d2aa20e6a490}{vrealloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align\+\_\+noprof()}. Otherwise, it calls \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a1956cee497c6e0aa3b0e0d61842c2b0c}{krealloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align\+\_\+noprof()}. If the krealloc fails, it falls back to \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a602b13cebb7df2d1fc1da9db991314dd}{kvmalloc\+\_\+node\+\_\+align\+\_\+noprof()} and copies the old data.

Function Description:\+ Reallocates memory using kvrealloc with alignment and node affinity without allocation profiling. It handles both kmalloc and vmalloc-\/backed memory. This is the internal implementation for kvrealloc.

Function Description:\+ This function atomically marks a slab as having failed to allocate object extensions. It uses cmpxchg() to set the slab-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}obj\+\_\+exts field to the special sentinel value OBJEXTS\+\_\+\+ALLOC\+\_\+\+FAIL only if it is currently 0 (uninitialized). The function returns true if the exchange succeeded (meaning it was the first failure and successfully marked the slab), or false if the field already contained a different value (either a valid pointer or already marked as failed). This allows the slab allocator to track which slabs have encountered extension allocation failures, enabling proper cleanup and handling of objects without metadata.

Function Description:\+ This function marks the code tag reference for a specific object as empty, which is used when an object is being freed or when its allocation tracking metadata needs to be cleared. It first retrieves the slab containing the object and its object extensions pointer (slab\+\_\+exts). If extensions exist, it gets the extension vector reference, calculates the object\textquotesingle{}s index within the slab using \doxylink{mm_2slab_8h_a7565efd517382aba5ed23fa18cd91337}{obj\+\_\+to\+\_\+index()}, and retrieves the specific \doxylink{structslabobj__ext}{slabobj\+\_\+ext} entry for that object. It then checks if the code tag reference is already empty using is\+\_\+codetag\+\_\+empty(); if so, it releases the extension reference and returns. Otherwise, it uses WARN\+\_\+\+ON() to catch any unexpected non-\/\+NULL code tag pointers (which would indicate inconsistent state), sets the reference to empty using set\+\_\+codetag\+\_\+empty(), and releases the extension reference. This function is critical for maintaining accurate allocation tracking (e.\+g., for memory accounting or debugging) when objects are freed, ensuring that stale metadata does not persist and cause false positives in memory leak detection or use-\/after-\/free analysis.

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{memcg\_slab\_post\_charge()}{memcg\_slab\_post\_charge()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_a891071a8ac46df323a73d1fe7f86dcde} 
bool memcg\+\_\+slab\+\_\+post\+\_\+charge (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{p}{, }\item[{gfp\+\_\+t}]{flags}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Function Description:\+ This function handles memcg (memory cgroup) charging for objects that were allocated without memcg charging (e.\+g., via \doxylink{slub_8c_a720e99cf4604474392f2669fef155930}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+charge()}). It first checks if the object is a large kmalloc allocation (Page\+Large\+Kmalloc). If so, and if the page is not already memcg-\/charged, it charges the entire page to the memcg using \doxylink{memcontrol_8h_a9d9a4b7caa926dbc04dfbe096812a51d}{\+\_\+\+\_\+memcg\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+charge\+\_\+page()}, then adjusts the global and memcg statistics by subtracting from global and adding to memcg to avoid double-\/counting. For normal slab objects, it retrieves the slab and cache, and skips charging for KMALLOC\+\_\+\+NORMAL caches to avoid circular dependencies. It then checks if the object already has a memcg extension (obj\+\_\+exts). If so, and the object is already charged (obj\+\_\+ext-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}objcg is non-\/\+NULL), it returns true. Otherwise, it calls \doxylink{memcontrol_8c_aba423f0bcd88afffb142a025d060c553}{\+\_\+\+\_\+memcg\+\_\+slab\+\_\+post\+\_\+alloc\+\_\+hook()} to perform the actual memcg charging. This function is called by \doxylink{slub_8c_a720e99cf4604474392f2669fef155930}{kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+charge()} to charge objects in cases where charging at allocation time was not possible (e.\+g., when the target memcg was not known at allocation time).

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{slub_8c_aa499af9d32044fdd4b23659d77ae26f6} 
bool need\+\_\+slab\+\_\+obj\+\_\+exts (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [inline]}, {\ttfamily [static]}}

Check if memory cgroup or memory allocation profiling is enabled. If enabled, SLUB tries to reduce memory overhead of accounting slab objects. If neither is enabled when this function is called, the optimization is simply skipped to avoid affecting caches that do not need \doxylink{structslabobj__ext}{slabobj\+\_\+ext} metadata.

However, this may disable optimization when memory cgroup or memory allocation profiling is used, but slabs are created too early even before those subsystems are initialized.

Function Description:\+ Checks if a slab cache needs object extensions for memcg or allocation profiling. Returns true if memcg accounting or allocation profiling is enabled for the cache.

Calculate the allocation size for \doxylink{structslabobj__ext}{slabobj\+\_\+ext} array.

When memory allocation profiling is enabled, the obj\+\_\+exts array could be allocated from the same slab cache it\textquotesingle{}s being allocated for. This would prevent the slab from ever being freed because it would always contain at least one allocated object (its own obj\+\_\+exts array).

To avoid this, increase the allocation size when we detect the array may come from the same cache, forcing it to use a different cache.

Function Description:\+ This helper function calculates the appropriate allocation size for storing slab object extensions (such as memcg or alloc tagging metadata) for objects in a slab. It first computes the required size as sizeof(struct slabobj\+\_\+ext) \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} slab-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}objects. For kmalloc caches (normal), it checks if the calculated size would fit into a standard kmalloc bucket by calling \doxylink{mm_2slab_8h_a35c83e79ace64317dc7857607c5d5941}{kmalloc\+\_\+slab()} to determine the cache that would serve this allocation. If the calculated size matches the object size of the kmalloc cache (meaning it would be exactly one object per slab), it returns object\+\_\+size + 1 to force the allocation into a larger bucket, preventing confusion between object data and extension metadata that could lead to memory corruption. If the size is too large for kmalloc or the cache is not a normal kmalloc cache, it returns the original calculated size. This ensures that extension metadata is stored safely without conflicting with object boundaries or causing slab layout issues.

Function Description:\+ Processes all objects in a slab to track their allocation or free locations. It uses a bitmap to identify which objects are currently allocated. For each allocated object, it retrieves the tracking information (track) and calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a65f54d04c232621b57f1506d56b28459}{add\+\_\+location()} to add that location to the tracking structure. This is used to build lists of allocation or free locations for debugging.

Function Description:\+ This function is the RCU callback for freeing a sheaf that was queued for deferred freeing. It prepares the sheaf by potentially removing objects that shouldn\textquotesingle{}t be freed (e.\+g., due to debugging hooks). It then attempts to put the sheaf back into the barn as a full sheaf. If the barn is at its full capacity, it flushes the sheaf, discarding its objects. If the sheaf becomes empty and the barn has room for empty sheaves, it is placed there; otherwise, it is completely freed.

Function Description:\+ This is the main function for refilling an array of objects from the slab allocator\textquotesingle{}s slow path. It first tries to get objects from the local node\textquotesingle{}s partial list. If that doesn\textquotesingle{}t fill the minimum required, it tries remote nodes. If still not enough, it allocates new slabs using \doxylink{slub_8c_ae1da11965135fb966370906c07198c04}{new\+\_\+slab()} and fills objects from them. Inlined fastpath so that allocation functions (kmalloc, kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+alloc) have the fastpath folded into their functions. So no function call overhead for requests that can be satisfied on the fastpath.

The fastpath works by first checking if the lockless freelist can be used. If not then \+\_\+\+\_\+slab\+\_\+alloc is called for slow processing.

Otherwise we can simply pick the next object from the lockless free list.

Function Description:\+ Main allocation function with fast/\+slow path selection. Handles KFENCE and post-\/allocation hooks. Returns the object or NULL.

Function Description:\+ This is the initialization function for the SLUB debugfs interface, called at boot time via an \+\_\+\+\_\+initcall. It creates the root debugfs directory /\+sys/\+kernel/\+debug/\+slab by calling debugfs\+\_\+create\+\_\+dir(). It then iterates over all existing slab caches in the system and, for each cache that has the SLAB\+\_\+\+STORE\+\_\+\+USER flag enabled (indicating it stores allocation/\+free tracking information), calls \doxylink{slub_8c_ada7ef7798e1a873b4a1ba405943d2349}{debugfs\+\_\+slab\+\_\+add()} to create per-\/cache debugfs files (typically alloc\+\_\+traces and free\+\_\+traces). These debugfs files provide detailed tracking information about object allocations and frees, which is invaluable for debugging memory leaks and use-\/after-\/free issues.

Function Description:\+ This function processes a freelist of objects being freed in bulk. It takes the head and tail of the list and the count, and applies \doxylink{slub_8c_a232beb6a2fef05c644a440a3907a321d}{slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+hook()} to each object. It first checks if the head is a KFENCE address; if so, it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a232beb6a2fef05c644a440a3907a321d}{slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+hook()} on it and returns false. It then reconstructs a new freelist by iterating through the objects. For each object, it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a232beb6a2fef05c644a440a3907a321d}{slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+hook()}; if the hook returns true (meaning the object can be freed immediately), it adds the object to the new freelist using \doxylink{slub_8c_aeba21275322f596f4c4796705bc2c4e2}{set\+\_\+freepointer()}. If the hook returns false (object\textquotesingle{}s reuse is delayed), it decrements the count. The function then sets the head and tail pointers to the reconstructed freelist and returns true if there are any objects left. This ensures that objects whose freeing is delayed (e.\+g., by KASAN quarantine or SLUB\+\_\+\+RCU\+\_\+\+DEBUG) are removed from the batch, while the rest are prepared for the actual \doxylink{slub_8c_a7538fb31a45f2685eb03ef2c5c42ef78}{\+\_\+\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free()} operation.

\+\_\+\+\_\+always\+\_\+inline bool slab\+\_\+free\+\_\+hook (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structkmem__cache}{kmem\+\_\+cache}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{s}{, }\item[{void \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{x}{, }\item[{bool}]{init}{, }\item[{bool}]{after\+\_\+rcu\+\_\+delay}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

Hooks for other subsystems that check memory allocations. In a typical production configuration these hooks all should produce no code at all.

Returns true if freeing of the object can proceed, false if its reuse was delayed by CONFIG\+\_\+\+SLUB\+\_\+\+RCU\+\_\+\+DEBUG or KASAN quarantine, or it was returned to KFENCE.

For objects allocated via \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a5869820842a9951b09600f4ee9f838d9}{kmalloc\+\_\+nolock()}, only a subset of alloc hooks are invoked, so some free hooks must handle asymmetric hook calls.

Alloc hooks called for \doxylink{include_2linux_2slab_8h_a5869820842a9951b09600f4ee9f838d9}{kmalloc\+\_\+nolock()}:\+
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item kmsan\+\_\+slab\+\_\+alloc()
\item kasan\+\_\+slab\+\_\+alloc()
\item \doxylink{slub_8c_ab74e8750ecbabab03f6a993eb41678f5}{memcg\+\_\+slab\+\_\+post\+\_\+alloc\+\_\+hook()}
\item \doxylink{slub_8c_a85cba6bfb1c77c44671d84b0c5644792}{alloc\+\_\+tagging\+\_\+slab\+\_\+alloc\+\_\+hook()}
\end{DoxyItemize}

Free hooks that must handle missing corresponding alloc hooks:\+
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item kmemleak\+\_\+free\+\_\+recursive()
\item kfence\+\_\+free()
\end{DoxyItemize}

Free hooks that have no alloc hook counterpart, and thus safe to call:\+
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item debug\+\_\+check\+\_\+no\+\_\+locks\+\_\+freed()
\item debug\+\_\+check\+\_\+no\+\_\+obj\+\_\+freed()
\item \+\_\+\+\_\+kcsan\+\_\+check\+\_\+access()
\end{DoxyItemize}

Function Description:\+ This is a critical hook called before freeing an object. It performs various checks and cleanup operations to ensure safe freeing. It calls kmemleak\+\_\+free\+\_\+recursive() to tell kmemleak to stop tracking the object, kmsan\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free() to handle KMSAN shadow state, and debug\+\_\+check\+\_\+no\+\_\+locks\+\_\+freed() and debug\+\_\+check\+\_\+no\+\_\+obj\+\_\+freed() to check for lock or object debug issues. If the object is not SLAB\+\_\+\+TYPESAFE\+\_\+\+BY\+\_\+\+RCU (or is being freed after an RCU delay), it uses KCSAN to help debug racy use-\/after-\/free. It then checks for KFENCE objects (returning false if handled), and gives KASAN a chance to notice invalid frees via kasan\+\_\+slab\+\_\+pre\+\_\+free(). If SLAB\+\_\+\+TYPESAFE\+\_\+\+BY\+\_\+\+RCU is enabled and the object is still accessible (not after an RCU delay), it attempts to allocate a \doxylink{structrcu__delayed__free}{rcu\+\_\+delayed\+\_\+free} structure and call call\+\_\+rcu() to delay freeing, returning false. If initialization on free is requested (init is true), it zeroes the object (using memset) while preserving the original size and redzone information, then restores the original size. Finally, it calls kasan\+\_\+slab\+\_\+free() to handle KASAN quarantine, returning true if the object can proceed to the actual free operation. This function returns false if the object\textquotesingle{}s reuse is delayed (by RCU or KASAN quarantine) or if it was returned to KFENCE.

Function Description:\+ This function is a memory hotplug callback for when a node is going offline. It iterates over all caches, flushes their per-\/\+CPU caches, and calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a3bb23c94982e9786c912475c939e55dc}{\+\_\+\+\_\+kmem\+\_\+cache\+\_\+do\+\_\+shrink()} for each cache to free memory on the node being removed. This helps ensure that no slab objects are left on a node that is going away.

Function Description:\+ This is a memory hotplug notifier callback that handles node online and offline events for the slab allocator. When a node is being brought online (with NODE\+\_\+\+ADDING\+\_\+\+FIRST\+\_\+\+MEMORY action), it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_ad39c38826bb5717a7630f638a196fdbb}{slab\+\_\+mem\+\_\+going\+\_\+online\+\_\+callback()} to allocate and initialize per-\/node structures for all existing caches on the new node. When a node is being taken offline (with NODE\+\_\+\+REMOVING\+\_\+\+LAST\+\_\+\+MEMORY action), it calls \doxylink{slub_8c_a512be0d46613a3af8c70ead82fe15e0d}{slab\+\_\+mem\+\_\+going\+\_\+offline\+\_\+callback()} to flush caches and shrink slabs on the node being removed. The function converts any error return value to a notifier error code using notifier\+\_\+from\+\_\+errno(), or returns NOTIFY\+\_\+\+OK on success. This ensures that the slab allocator properly manages its per-\/node data structures as the system\textquotesingle{}s memory topology changes during hotplug operations.

Variable Description:\+ This is a struct kernel\+\_\+param\+\_\+ops that defines the operations for the slab\+\_\+debug kernel parameter (and its alias slub\+\_\+debug). It has the KERNEL\+\_\+\+PARAM\+\_\+\+OPS\+\_\+\+FL\+\_\+\+NOARG flag set, indicating the parameter takes no argument (it\textquotesingle{}s a boolean flag), and specifies the set function as setup\+\_\+slub\+\_\+debug. This allows users to enable or configure SLUB debugging features (such as red zoning, poisoning, tracking, and consistency checks) via the kernel command line, which is essential for diagnosing memory corruption issues, detecting use-\/after-\/free bugs, and validating slab allocator behavior during development and testing.

Variable Description:\+ This is a struct kernel\+\_\+param\+\_\+ops that defines the operations for the slab\+\_\+min\+\_\+order and slub\+\_\+min\+\_\+order kernel parameters. It specifies the set function as setup\+\_\+slub\+\_\+min\+\_\+order, which is called when the parameter is set at boot time or via the kernel command line. This allows users to control the minimum page order (allocation size) for slab caches.

Variable Description:\+ This is a struct kernel\+\_\+param\+\_\+ops that defines the operations for the slab\+\_\+max\+\_\+order and slub\+\_\+max\+\_\+order kernel parameters. It specifies the set function as setup\+\_\+slub\+\_\+max\+\_\+order, which is called when the parameter is set. This allows users to control the maximum page order for slab allocations, with the handler ensuring the value does not exceed MAX\+\_\+\+PAGE\+\_\+\+ORDER and adjusting slub\+\_\+min\+\_\+order if necessary to maintain consistency.

Variable Description:\+ This is a struct kernel\+\_\+param\+\_\+ops that defines the operations for the slab\+\_\+strict\+\_\+numa kernel parameter. It has the KERNEL\+\_\+\+PARAM\+\_\+\+OPS\+\_\+\+FL\+\_\+\+NOARG flag set, indicating it takes no argument, and specifies the set function as setup\+\_\+slab\+\_\+strict\+\_\+numa. This allows enabling strict NUMA allocation behavior for the slab allocator via a kernel command line option, which helps enforce local node allocations and reduce remote memory accesses.

Variable Description:\+ This is a struct file\+\_\+operations structure that defines the operations for the slab debugfs trace files. It specifies the handler functions for opening (slab\+\_\+debug\+\_\+trace\+\_\+open), reading (seq\+\_\+read -\/ the standard seq\+\_\+file read handler), seeking (seq\+\_\+lseek -\/ standard seq\+\_\+file seek handler), and releasing (slab\+\_\+debug\+\_\+trace\+\_\+release) the file. This structure is used when creating the alloc\+\_\+traces and free\+\_\+traces debugfs files, allowing userspace to read allocation/\+free tracking information from the kernel through a simple file interface using the seq\+\_\+file API for convenient sequential reading.
